    80:         mode: "0755"
    81:         force: True
    82:       when: cargo_exists_result is failed
    83: 
    84:     - name: Install rust/cargo (recommended way)

    86:       when: cargo_exists_result is failed

    88:     - name: Make rustc and cargo available for pip

    91:         dest: "/usr/local/bin/{{ item }}"

    95:         state: link

    99:         - "cargo"

    26:     # The cache is an HA pair (tofu node_services generates one instance per
    27:     # always-on node; all carry the `apt-cache` tag, so apt_cacher_group tracks
    28:     # them with no inventory change here). apt itself supports only a single
    29:     # Acquire::http::Proxy value, so instance selection uses apt's native
    30:     # Proxy-Auto-Detect hook instead: at every apt run the script probes each
    31:     # instance by FQDN and prints the first live one, or DIRECT so apt fails
    32:     # open when the whole pool is down. An instance (or its node) going down
    33:     # therefore costs one probe timeout, never apt itself.
    34:     - name: Deploy apt proxy autodetect script
    35:       when: groups['apt_cacher_group'] | default([]) | length > 0
    36:       vars:
    37:         _apt_cache_port: >-
    38:           {{ tofu_data.constants.service_ports.apt_cacher_ng
    39:              | default(3142) }}
    40:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    41:         dest: /usr/local/bin/apt-proxy-detect
    42:         content: |
    43:           #!/bin/bash
    44:           # Managed by Ansible (ansible-proxmox-apps site.yml) — do not edit.
    45:           # apt Acquire::http::Proxy-Auto-Detect hook: first live cache wins,
    46:           # DIRECT when none answer (fail open, apt fetches upstream).
    47:           for host in {% for h in groups['apt_cacher_group'] | sort -%}
    48:           {{ h }}.{{ tofu_data.domain }} {% endfor %}; do
    49:             if timeout 2 bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${host}/{{ _apt_cache_port }}" 2>/dev/null; then
    50:               exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
    51:               echo "http://${host}:{{ _apt_cache_port }}"
    52:               exit 0
    53:             fi
    54:           done
    55:           echo DIRECT

name: Decide renewal from the certificate deployed on the host
review_question: Is this Ansible play excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
25: #   Optional inputs (CLI/inventory): letsencrypt_force_issue,
    26: #     acme_keys_path, acme_certificate_renewal_on_remaining_days
    27: #   letsencrypt_*  - the renewal decision (needs_issue, remaining_days)
    28: #   _*             - playbook-internal plumbing (paths, names, env, registers)
    29: 
    30: - name: Decide renewal from the certificate deployed on the host
    31:   hosts: "{{ cert_hosts | default('letsencrypt') }}"
    32:   gather_facts: false
    33:   become: true
    34: 
    35:   vars:
    36:     _run_user: "{{ linux_podman_run_as_user | default('igou') }}"
    37:     _fullchain_secret: "{{ linux_tls_fullchain_secret | default('tls-fullchain') }}"
    38:     _renew_days: "{{ acme_certificate_renewal_on_remaining_days | default(15) }}"
    39:     _rootless_env:
    40:       XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: "/run/user/{{ getent_passwd[_run_user][1] }}"
    41:       HOME: "/home/{{ _run_user }}"
    42: 
    43:   tasks:
    44:     - name: Resolve the run user's uid (for the rootless podman runtime dir)
    45:       ansible.builtin.getent:
    46:         database: passwd
    47:         key: "{{ _run_user }}"
    48: 
    49:     - name: List the run user's podman secrets
    50:       containers.podman.podman_secret_info:
    51:       become: true
    52:       become_user: "{{ _run_user }}"
    53:       environment: "{{ _rootless_env }}"
    54:       register: _secrets
    55:       changed_when: false
    56: 
    57:     - name: Read the deployed certificate (when the secret exists)
    58:       containers.podman.podman_secret_info:
    59:         name: "{{ _fullchain_secret }}"
    60:         showsecret: true
    61:       become: true
    62:       become_user: "{{ _run_user }}"
    63:       environment: "{{ _rootless_env }}"
    64:       register: _deployed
    65:       changed_when: false
    66:       when: _fullchain_secret in (_secrets.secrets | map(attribute='Spec.Name') | list)
    67: 
    68:     - name: Read the deployed certificate's expiry
    69:       community.crypto.x509_certificate_info:
    70:         content: "{{ _deployed.secrets[0].SecretData }}"
    71:       delegate_to: localhost
    72:       # The play's become:true must not follow the delegation - parsing a cert
    73:       # needs no privilege and the EE has no sudo.
    74:       become: false
    75:       vars:
    76:         # The inventory's localhost host has no ansible_connection set (it
    77:         # defaults to ssh, intentionally - armbian builds SSH back into it), so
    78:         # a bare delegate_to: localhost tries to ssh into the EE, which has no
    79:         # sshd. Force local here; never pin it on the inventory host itself.
    80:         ansible_connection: local
    81:         ansible_python_interpreter: "{{ ansible_playbook_python }}"
    82:       register: _cert
    83:       when: _deployed is not skipped
    84: 
    85:     - name: Compute days remaining on the deployed certificate
    86:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    87:         letsencrypt_remaining_days: >-
    88:           {{ ((_cert.not_after | ansible.builtin.to_datetime('%Y%m%d%H%M%SZ')) - now(utc=true)).days
    89:              if (_deployed is not skipped) else -1 }}
    90: 
    91:     - name: Decide whether to issue a new certificate
    92:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    93:         letsencrypt_needs_issue: >-
    94:           {{ (letsencrypt_force_issue | default(false) | bool)
    95:              or (_deployed is skipped)
    96:              or ((letsencrypt_remaining_days | int) < (_renew_days | int)) }}
    97: 
    98:     - name: Report the decision
    99:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   100:         msg: >-
   101:           {{ 'No certificate deployed; bootstrapping.' if (_deployed is skipped)
   102:              else (letsencrypt_remaining_days ~ ' day(s) remaining; '
   103:                    ~ ('renewing.' if (letsencrypt_needs_issue | bool) else 'within threshold, skipping.')) }}
   104: 
   105: # We drive the ACME order with the community.crypto split-order modules instead
   106: # of the felixfontein.acme role, because a wildcard + apex cert needs TWO TXT
   107: # values at the single name _acme-challenge.<domain>, and the role's Cloudflare
   108: # provider writes only value[0] with solo:true (deleting the other). Here the
   109: # "Publish" task loops over EVERY challenge value, using solo only on the first
   110: # per record (clears stale, then appends) - the multi-value handling Cloudflare
   111: # needs. TXT records are torn down in always:, even if validation fails.
   112: - name: Issue the certificate on the control node (Cloudflare DNS-01)
   113:   hosts: "{{ cert_hosts | default('letsencrypt') }}"
   114:   gather_facts: false
   115:   connection: local
   116:   become: false
   117: 
   118:   vars:
   119:     # This play runs locally but targets the remote host, whose discovered
   120:     # interpreter would otherwise be used; pin to the controller's interpreter.
   121:     ansible_python_interpreter: "{{ ansible_playbook_python }}"
   122:     _keys_path: "{{ acme_keys_path | default('/tmp/acme-' ~ inventory_hostname) }}"
   123:     _cert_basename: "{{ letsencrypt_cert_domains[0] | replace('*', '_') }}"
   124:     _acme_directory: "{{ letsencrypt_acme_directory | default('https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory') }}"
   125: 
   126:   tasks:
   127:     - name: Nothing to issue when no renewal is needed
   128:       ansible.builtin.meta: end_host
   129:       when: not (letsencrypt_needs_issue | default(false) | bool)
   130: 
   131:     # Resolve each 1Password secret exactly ONCE. As play vars these lookups are
   132:     # lazy and re-run on every reference (and every loop item), bursting the 1P
   133:     # service-account rate limit; materialize them up front and reuse the facts.
   134:     # The shared ACME account is read on the control node only (never reaches
   135:     # the host).
   136:     - name: Resolve issuance secrets from 1Password (once)
   137:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   138:         _account_content: "{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'acme-key', field='key.b64', vault='lab_external_api_keys') | b64decode }}"
   139:         _account_email: "{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'acme-key', field='email', vault='lab_external_api_keys') }}"
   140:         _cf_token: "{{ acme_certificate_cloudflare_token }}"
   141:       no_log: true
   142: 
   143:     - name: Ensure the scratch keys directory exists on the control node
   144:       ansible.builtin.file:
   145:         path: "{{ _keys_path }}"
   146:         state: directory
   147:         mode: "0700"
   148: 
   149:     # Fresh keypair each issuance - keys_path is a throwaway scratch dir, so no
   150:     # private key persists on the controller (the delivery play removes it).
   151:     - name: Generate the certificate private key
   152:       community.crypto.openssl_privatekey:
   153:         path: "{{ _keys_path }}/{{ _cert_basename }}.key"
   154:         type: RSA
   155:         size: 4096
   156:         mode: "0600"
   157:         force: true
   158: 
   159:     - name: Generate the CSR with all SANs (wildcard + apex)
   160:       community.crypto.openssl_csr:
   161:         path: "{{ _keys_path }}/{{ _cert_basename }}.csr"
   162:         privatekey_path: "{{ _keys_path }}/{{ _cert_basename }}.key"
   163:         subject_alt_name: "{{ letsencrypt_cert_domains | map('regex_replace', '^(.*)$', 'DNS:\\1') | list }}"
   164:         use_common_name_for_san: false
   165: 
   166:     - name: Ensure the shared ACME account exists (terms agreed)
   167:       community.crypto.acme_account:
   168:         account_key_content: "{{ _account_content }}"
   169:         contact: ["mailto:{{ _account_email }}"]
   170:         terms_agreed: true
   171:         allow_creation: true
   172:         state: present
   173:         acme_directory: "{{ _acme_directory }}"
   174:         acme_version: 2
   175: 
   176:     - name: Create the ACME order and read the DNS-01 challenges
   177:       community.crypto.acme_certificate_order_create:
   178:         account_key_content: "{{ _account_content }}"
   179:         csr: "{{ _keys_path }}/{{ _cert_basename }}.csr"
   180:         acme_directory: "{{ _acme_directory }}"
   181:         acme_version: 2
   182:       register: _order
   183: 
   184:     # challenge_data_dns is {record_name: [values...]}; apex + wildcard collapse
   185:     # to one _acme-challenge.<domain> key whose list holds BOTH tokens.
   186:     - name: Publish, validate, then always tear down the challenge records
   187:       block:
   188:         - name: Publish every challenge TXT value to Cloudflare
   189:           community.general.cloudflare_dns:
   190:             api_token: "{{ _cf_token }}"

source_context:
35: # SHA for a fully deterministic build across both kustomize stages.
    36: #
    37: #   KUBECONFIG=... OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=ops_... \
    38: #     ansible-playbook playbooks/kubernetes/bootstrap-gitops.yaml \
    39: #     [-e gitops_ref=master] [-e gitops_cluster=internal]
    40: - name: Bootstrap cluster GitOps from igou-kubernetes
    41:   hosts: localhost
    42:   connection: local
    43:   gather_facts: false
    44: 
    45:   vars:
    46:     # Base URL for the kustomize remote-build `//<path>?ref=` form (no `.git`).
    47:     gitops_repo: https://github.com/igou-io/igou-kubernetes
    48:     gitops_ref: master
    49:     gitops_cluster: internal
    50:     connect_secret_namespace: external-secrets
    51:     connect_secret_name: onepassword-connect-token
    52:     # rk8s entity Connect token: `rk8s_connect_token_lookup` (igou-inventory
    53:     # group_vars/all/main.yml) carries the full 1Password lookup expression,
    54:     # read via the read-only ocp-bootstrap SA (same as
    55:     # playbooks/openshift/bootstrap_gitops.yaml).
    56: 
    57:   tasks:
    58:     - name: Assert KUBECONFIG and the bootstrap service-account token are present
    59:       # OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN feeds the community.general.onepassword env
    60:       # fallback used by the token-seed task below. vars_prompt is NOT used: it
    61:       # silently returns empty under ansible-navigator/AAP (no interactive TTY
    62:       # wired to the lookup), which makes the lookup fall through to an
    63:       # interactive sign-in and fail with "Missing required parameters".
    64:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    65:         that:
    66:           - lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'KUBECONFIG') | length > 0
    67:           - lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN') | length > 0
    68:         fail_msg: >-
    69:           KUBECONFIG and OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN must be set. Point KUBECONFIG
    70:           at the target cluster and export the ocp-bootstrap service-account
    71:           token (ops_...), e.g. `export OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=ops_...` (AAP
    72:           injects it via a credential).
    73: 
    74:     - name: Ensure the external-secrets namespace exists
    75:       kubernetes.core.k8s:
    76:         state: present
    77:         definition:
    78:           apiVersion: v1
    79:           kind: Namespace
    80:           metadata:
    81:             name: "{{ connect_secret_namespace }}"
    82: 
    83:     - name: Seed the rk8s entity Connect token secret (for ESO)
    84:       kubernetes.core.k8s:
    85:         state: present
    86:         # force_conflicts: ESO/argocd may later own this Secret; a re-seed
    87:         # must win the field ownership back to reconcile the Connect token.
    88:         server_side_apply:
    89:           field_manager: ansible
    90:           force_conflicts: true
    91:         definition:
    92:           apiVersion: v1
    93:           kind: Secret
    94:           metadata:
    95:             name: "{{ connect_secret_name }}"
    96:             namespace: "{{ connect_secret_namespace }}"
    97:             annotations:
    98:               managed-by: ansible
    99:           type: Opaque
   100:           stringData:
   101:             # rk8s ENTITY Connect token from ocp-connect-bootstrap, read via the
   102:             # ocp-bootstrap SA (OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN env fallback) — NOT the
   103:             # kubeconfig-read token. Same pattern as openshift/bootstrap_gitops.yaml.
   104:             token: "{{ rk8s_connect_token_lookup }}"
   105:       no_log: true
   106: 
   107:     - name: Install argocd (server-side apply)
   108:       # One-shot per bootstrap: no force_conflicts here (unlike the token seed
   109:       # above). Once argocd self-adopts its own install, a re-run conflicts on
   110:       # field ownership and fails loudly — safer than ansible silently
   111:       # reclaiming fields argocd now manages.
   112:       kubernetes.core.k8s:
   113:         state: present
   114:         server_side_apply:
   115:           field_manager: ansible
   116:         definition: "{{ lookup('kubernetes.core.kustomize', dir=gitops_repo ~ '//components/argocd?ref=' ~ gitops_ref, enable_helm=true) }}"
   117: 
   118:     - name: Wait for argocd server rollout
   119:       kubernetes.core.k8s_info:
   120:         api_version: apps/v1
   121:         kind: Deployment
   122:         name: argocd-server
   123:         namespace: argocd
   124:         wait: true
   125:         wait_condition:
   126:           type: Available
   127:           status: "True"
   128:         wait_timeout: 300
   129: 
   130:     - name: Apply the cluster root ({{ gitops_cluster }})
   131:       # namespace: argocd — the cluster root's Application/AppProject CRs carry
   132:       # no metadata.namespace (argo's own sync places them via the app-of-apps
   133:       # destination); without it they land in `default` where argocd never sees
   134:       # them.
   135:       kubernetes.core.k8s:
   136:         state: present
   137:         namespace: argocd
   138:         definition: "{{ lookup('kubernetes.core.kustomize', dir=gitops_repo ~ '//clusters/' ~ gitops_cluster ~ '?ref=' ~ gitops_ref, enable_helm=true) }}"
   139:       register: _root_apply
   140:       retries: 50
   141:       delay: 15
   142:       until: _root_apply is succeeded

   144:     - name: Report bootstrap result
   145:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   146:         verbosity: 1
   147:         msg: >-
   148:           Bootstrapped {{ gitops_cluster }} from {{ gitops_repo }}@{{ gitops_ref }};
   149:           argocd now self-manages the cluster.

    16:     - name: Allow access to Traefik entry points
    17:       ansible.posix.firewalld:

    32:         - port: "{{ traefik_dokku_ssh_port.port }}/{{ traefik_dokku_ssh_port.protocol }}"
    33: 
    34:     - name: Configure passive FTP port forwarding

    36:         - name: Clear stale firewall rules
    37:           ansible.builtin.shell:
    38:             executable: /bin/bash
    39:             cmd: |
    40:               set -e
    41:               IFS=$'\n'
    42: 
    43:               current_rules=$(firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --get-all-rules | grep "{{ ftp_firewall_rules_tag }}_" || true)
    44:               for rule in $current_rules; do
    45:                 rule_name=$(echo "$rule" | awk '{print $NF}' | sed 's/{{ ftp_firewall_rules_tag }}_//')
    46:                 if ! echo "{{ ftp_firewall_rules | map(attribute='name') | list }}" | grep -q "'$rule_name'"; then
    47:                   # `$rule` cannot be passed directly to remove the rule because it will be treated as a
    48:                   # single argument, so split it into an array to pass each part as a separate argument
    49:                   IFS=' ' read -r -a rule_parts <<< "$rule"
    50:                   firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --remove-rule "${rule_parts[@]}"
    51:                   echo "Rule removed: '$rule_name'"
    52:                 fi
    53:               done
    54:           register: ftp_firewall_rules_cleanup
    55:           changed_when: "'Rule removed' in ftp_firewall_rules_cleanup.stdout"
    56: 
    57:         - name: Deploy firewall rules
    58:           ansible.builtin.shell:
    59:             executable: /bin/bash
    60:             cmd: |
    61:               set -e
    62: 
    63:               existing_rule=$(firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --get-all-rules | grep "{{ ftp_firewall_rules_tag }}_{{ item.name }}$" || true)
    64:               if [[ -n "$existing_rule" ]]; then
    65:                 firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --remove-rule $existing_rule
    66:               fi
    67: 
    68:               firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --add-rule {{ item.rule }} -m comment --comment "{{ ftp_firewall_rules_tag }}_{{ item.name }}"
    69:               new_rule=$(firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --get-all-rules | grep "{{ ftp_firewall_rules_tag }}_{{ item.name }}$")

    71:               if [[ "$new_rule" != "$existing_rule" ]]; then
    72:                 echo "Rule changed: '{{ item.name }}'"
    73:               fi

    75:           loop_control:
    76:             label: "{{ item.name }}"

    78:           changed_when: "'Rule changed' in ftp_firewall_rules_deploy.stdout"
